claims.claim: Transmissions Gearbox M278 1282 OEM G63, Mercedes transmission gearbox.
claims.evidence: Witness photos show a used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly with dirt/scuffs, but make/model/part number (M278/1282) and G63 compatibility are not readable.
No photo evidence of prior operation, test results, or running condition; internal condition is only visually inferred from grime/wear.

risks.risk: Wrong make/model/part number or wrong fitment for the buyer’s vehicle (compatibility not confirmable from the photos).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the transmission identification/part number label or stamping (including OEM number) and the vehicle VIN/vehicle details it came from.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as an unknown/possibly incompatible used automatic transmission (worst-case fitment risk).

risks.risk: Incomplete assembly (missing sensors/solenoids/valve body components/wiring connectors/bolts) which can prevent installation or proper operation.
risks.proof: A full laid-out inventory photo showing all external components included (solenoids/sensors/connectors/hoses/bolts) plus a photo of the transmission pan/valve body area if accessible.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially incomplete used unit (worst-case missing parts).

risks.risk: Not working / internal damage (clutch packs, torque converter, pump wear) despite appearance.
risks.proof: Video of the transmission being tested/bench-tested (or at minimum a start-in-vehicle video showing engagement and smooth shifting) before removal, plus any diagnostic codes if available.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as non-verified working condition (worst-case treated as not working).

risks.risk: Oil leaks or seal/gasket failure (seepage not confirmable from the provided shots).
risks.proof: Photos showing the unit after cleaning with no fresh oil, close-ups of gasket/seal areas, and a leak check (wipe test) or evidence of oil level/condition.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as may require reseal/repair (worst-case leak/seal issues).

risks.risk: Heavy grime and surface damage could indicate prior overheating or rough handling, increasing repair likelihood.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of any discoloration (burn marks), cracks, bent mounting points, and the bell housing/torque converter mating surfaces; plus a photo of the underside for impact damage.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst-case wear/possible overheating/repair needed based on visible grime and scuffs.

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up photo of the transmission’s OEM part number/label/stamping (must be readable).
Send photos showing all included external components: sensors, solenoids, wiring connectors, valve body/solenoid pack area (if accessible), and all mounting bolts/parts included.
Provide proof it worked before removal: short video of shifting/engagement in the vehicle or a bench-test report/result.
Show leak/seal condition: photos after wiping/cleaning, close-ups of gasket/seal areas, and confirm no fresh seepage.
Share the vehicle details it came from (make/model/year and drivetrain) and/or VIN so compatibility can be verified.
response.reason: The witness can identify it as a used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly, so it can be priced at its worst-case as an unverified, possibly incomplete/possibly non-working unit with unknown compatibility. Seller claims about exact Mercedes M278/1282 G63 fitment and perfect working status are not verifiable from the photos.
